response.query: How will privacy-preserving methods (differential privacy, federated learning, synthetic data) impact model utility, and what minimum utility is acceptable?
response.answer: Privacy-preserving methods like differential privacy, federated learning, and synthetic data can reduce model utility but often maintain acceptable performance. Minimum acceptable utility varies by application but generally aims for 80-90% of non-private model performance.

results.title: Synthetic data for privacy-preserving clinical risk prediction
results.content: We further quantify the usefulness of hyperparameter tuning on synthetic data in Table 2, where we report the improvement in model discrimination (C-index) on the real test dataset \(\mathbb {D}^{r}\_{test}\). Under real-world data release assumptions, synthetic data generated with existing privacy-preserving algorithms from large scale biobanks can effectively support the development of prognostic models for the 5-year risk of lung cancer. Furthermore, the hyperparameters selected for a deep learning model trained on synthetic data were similar to the real dataset, particularly across those hyperparameters such as model \(\alpha\), \(\sigma\), and dropout rate, that most impact model performance. To explore the usefulness of synthetic data for model training, we used the train-on-synthetic, test-on-real approach in which we fitted a Cox regression model on the synthetic data, \(\mathbb {D}^{s}\), with all candidate prognostic features and then evaluate its performance on the real, test, dataset (\(\mathbb {D}^{r}\_{test}\)).

results.title: Abstract
results.content: Overall, client-level DP-FL can deliver useful county-level predictions with strong privacy guarantees, and viable privacy budgets depend on epidemic phase, allowing privacy-compliant collaboration among health authorities for local forecasting. In the context of federated learning, several foundational works have combined -DP with standard federated learning algorithms that aggregate client updates on a central server [25, 26, 27], or with local differential privacy mechanisms in which each client perturbs its model update before sending it to the server [28]. We developed a differential privacy-preserving federated learning approach for predicting COVID-19 case numbers on a spatially resolved level and validated the approach on county-level for two different time periods, November 2020 and March 2022. For a privacy-preserving budget of , we were able to achieve predictions that closely match the quality of non-DP models, with an value of 0.88 for the 2022 data and 0.94 for the 2020 data.
